label: VStack
title: VStack
summary: Use VStack for page flow, grouped details, and ordered content. Its children follow token-driven spacing and padding while the host supplies the available height.
corePrinciple: Use vertical rhythm to show hierarchy. A constrained height can let wrapped children flow into columns; it does not turn VStack into a responsive grid.

anatomy.title: VStack has one job
anatomy.description: See the column, slot, rhythm, and inset in one live example.
blocks: Children follow a vertical page-flow order. Reverse is available when the content order genuinely needs it.
Slot gap sets the repeated rhythm between children and remains consistent as content grows.
Direct children share the owner’s cross-axis edge, while wrap flows into a new column only inside a height boundary.
Default or None comes from the component mode. Do not recreate its inset with local wrappers.

configuration.title: Configure the owner, then read the result
configuration.description: Choose vertical rhythm and inset once. Wrap is meaningful only inside a real height boundary.
blocks: Use the token rhythm that matches the surrounding hierarchy. Do not tune each child independently.
Default and None are owner modes. Choose None when a containing pattern already supplies the page inset.
VStack wraps into columns only when the host supplies a constrained height.
Storybook exposes gap, padding, stack context, background, and color mode contexts. This guide keeps the examples focused on choices that alter the visible flow.

states.title: VStack responds to its host
states.description: Compare default, changed rhythm, host-owned edge, and constrained outcomes without recreating the layout primitive.
blocks: VStack uses its default direction and token rhythm.
Changing the owner gap changes the whole group.
None lets a containing pattern own the edge inset.
Wrapping appears when the host supplies a constraint.
A stack is a layout result inside its parent. Make the container boundary and content order clear before changing gap or wrap.

sizing.title: The parent supplies the constraint
sizing.description: VStack wrap is a height outcome. Width alone does not turn a column into a grid.
blocks: VStack wraps into columns only when its height is constrained. Width alone does not make columns.

content.title: Make the relationship visible
content.description: Columns work when sequence and grouping make the page easier to read.
blocks: Use the column to make sequence, grouping, and supporting detail easy to scan.
Place related content in one slot so spacing stays contiguous as items change.
Only use wrap when the host has a real height boundary and columns are meaningful.
Use Default or None padding once. Avoid stacked insets from nested owners.

inContext.title: Place the primitive where the relationship happens
inContext.description: Use VStack for one coherent vertical group, from heading through supporting detail and next step.
blocks: Keep the page in one flow
Group a heading, supporting copy, and next step in a clear sequence.
A nested group can use None when the surrounding section owns the inset.
Let vertical rhythm do the explaining
Use a vertical stack for one coherent group so each gap carries meaning.

doDont.title: Protect structure and clarity
doDont.description: These pairs keep the layout relationship visible as content and host constraints change.
blocks: A single vertical flow keeps hierarchy and rhythm contiguous.
Use a giant gap to separate unrelated sections
Spacing cannot repair a missing grouping boundary or unclear content hierarchy.
Use None when the section owns the inset
The visible boundary has one clear owner and the content remains aligned.
Stack component insets without a reason
Nested owners can create an unintended double edge and weaken alignment.

sources.title: Grounded in the published component
sources.description: The guide separates designer choices from behavior supplied by the public library at runtime.
blocks: Live layout examples use public exports from jfs-components 0.1.60. VStack uses its public package export with token-driven modes; documentation controls change owner configuration, not component internals.
